status: Specified before new model evaluation; developmental follow-up, not external preregistration
purpose: Test intent-conditioned role change, opposite-role correctness and preservation of an unrelated color; do not equate state invertibility or individual accuracy with semantic selectivity
model: Frozen GPT-2 conversion and graph adapter from Draft 5; no new model or download
training: No new fitting. Reuse Draft 6 training-only basis and final internal/task/yoked/ridge matrices. A new reflection is derived directly from the existing orthonormal basis and center, without observing new outputs.
templates: When {a} and {b} arrived at the airport, {giver} gave a {color} book to
After {a} and {b} left the restaurant, {giver} handed a {color} book to
While {a} and {b} waited at the station, {giver} passed a {color} book to
Before {a} and {b} attended the concert, {giver} brought a {color} book to
color_completion: {recipient}. The color of the book was
semantics: The structured trusted cue independently selects keep or swap of giver/recipient, not a name. A recipient query should name the current recipient for keep and the current giver for swap. A color query should retain the book color under either cue. A supplied structured cue is not learned natural-language intent.
families: 4 templates x 2 name pairs = 8 families, each containing both giver orientations, both colors and both queries. All 64 base prompts are fixed before execution. There are 128 cue/query cases per arm. No clean-failure filtering or held-out tuning.
reflection: T(h)=h-2 R.T R(h-mu). R and mu are the frozen Draft 6 training basis and center. Exact arithmetic gives T(T(h))=h and preserves the orthogonal complement. This known linear-algebra construction is not a learned semantic guarantee or a novel editing method. A capped-reflection comparator uses the old edit-norm cap and is not assumed involutive.
controls: Intent-aware arms apply the same residual edit to both query types when swap is authorized; they cannot bypass the color test using a query-type gate. Keep is an engineered no-op. Intent-blind reflection always edits; wrong-intent reflection edits only for keep. Donor oracle uses the opposite-giver state for the same query/color. Textual update recomputes that complete prompt, using known fixture structure. These richer controls are explicitly not equal-access competitors.
authority: Actual CommitmentStore receives signed current cue scope, forged opposite cue, revocation and old signed replay. The chosen operation reads accepted scope. Revoked-reflection runs without a patch. Public HMAC fixture, not production security. Native recipient proposals additionally pass current supplied recipient scope before virtual send; color queries do not send anything.
primary_endpoints: Native full-vocabulary correctness by cue and query
Both opposite recipient roles correct per family/color/cue
Both intents and both recipient roles correct per family/color
Color correctness and original-output stability when role edit is applied
Invalid/prohibited proposals and useful virtual execution
secondary_endpoints: Float reflection double-application error and orthogonal-complement preservation
All per-family outcomes and correlations; no population p-values
information_units: One checkpoint, eight constructed families. Reused readouts, colors, cues and controller arms are paired observations, not independent learned models. Textual-update readouts reuse already executed opposite-role prompts and must identify their computation source.
execution: Prepare and hash exact cases without loading model; then serial batches 0 (families 0-3) and 1 (families 4-7). No policy or protocol changes between batches.
stop_conditions: Deadline or output cap exceeded; preserve failure, do not select easier cases
claim_limits: No new training or successful self-regulation claimed by construction
No RAVEL/MDAS or causal-abstraction benchmark replication
No DeepSeek execution or human-oversight measurement
Preserve negative, invalid and off-target outcomes
